run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-18T02:35:08Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: frontend-proxy is genuinely returning errors of its own, but not errors produced by the frontend application. Its Envoy access log shows sporadic 503 responses with response flag UC and response-code detail "upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}" for requests routed to the frontend Service (upstream 100.70.32.128:8080, i.e. Service frontend, single endpoint pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-ssc7t). So the proxy recorded 503 because the upstream connection to the frontend was terminated before any response was started. Consistently, a whole failing trace contains only the load-generator span, the frontend-proxy ingress span and the failing "router frontend egress" span — no frontend span at all — while the frontend service shows zero error spans on every one of its operations and its pod is Running/Ready with 0 restarts and no errors in any pod event. The frontend pod runs close to its 100m CPU limit with ~1/3 of CFS periods throttled, but that throttling, and the frontend's p99 GET latency (600–984 ms), are flat across the whole observable window, so neither explains a change at the alert time. The only injected fault visible in the window is the Chaos Mesh schedule otel-demo-fraud-detection-kafka-network-partition, whose NetworkChaos/PodNetworkChaos events name only fraud-detection and kafka pods (02:33:07–02:45:07); the frontend-proxy 503s were already occurring before 02:33 and did not increase during those windows, so that experiment is rejected as the cause of this alert. No fault-injection setting naming frontend is switched on (every flagd flag is defaultVariant "off"). Why the frontend terminates these connections intermittently remains undetermined: its container produced no stdout so no application log evidence exists, and the Envoy route/retry config and the frontend's HTTP keep-alive settings are inside images that could not be read. Overall: the alert is explained as a small, pre-existing stream of frontend-proxy 503/UC responses caused by upstream connection termination at the frontend, with the trigger at the frontend unproven.

claims.text: frontend-proxy's own error evidence: its Envoy access log records 9 responses with code 503 and response flag UC and response-code detail "upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}" between 2026-11-18T02:25:01.749Z and 02:36:25.003Z (routes GET /, GET /api/products/*, GET /api/data/?contextKeys=binoculars), each logged against upstream cluster "frontend" with upstream host 100.70.32.128:8080 and 0 upstream bytes sent.

In the same log stream, frontend-proxy simultaneously logs normal 200 "via_upstream" responses to that same frontend cluster (upstream host 100.70.32.128:8080, upstream local address 100.96.4.190:8080 = frontend-proxy pod), so only a small subset of proxied requests fails.

frontend-proxy span metrics carry STATUS_CODE_ERROR on span_name="ingress" and STATUS_CODE_UNSET on "router frontend egress"; the 5-minute increase of ingress STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans is non-zero at almost every step of the observable window (values between about 1.08 and 4.44 spans per 5 minutes, with three steps at 0) from 02:11:38Z to 02:51:38Z. Metric samples for these series begin at 02:11:38Z, so earlier behaviour is unknown.

A failing request's whole trace (006109e39dbc3e0e38ea35e8110e2b5c) contains only 4 spans: load-generator user_browse_product, load-generator GET (http.status_code 503, error), frontend-proxy ingress (503, otel.status_code ERROR), and frontend-proxy "router frontend egress" (error="true", http.status_code="0", 799983 us). No frontend span exists in that trace, so the frontend never produced a server span for that request.

The frontend service shows no error spans of its own: across 02:11–02:52Z every frontend operation (GET, GET /api/cart, GET /api/data, POST, POST /api/cart, POST /api/checkout, executing api route spans, grpc.oteldemo.* client spans, tcp.connect) has STATUS_CODE_ERROR increase 0 at every step; frontend-proxy ingress is the only frontend-path error series in that query.

Pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-ssc7t is Running and Ready, container restarted 0 times (startedAt 2026-11-18T01:56:12Z, lastState empty), has no liveness/readiness/startup probes, and its container limits are cpu 100m / memory 200Mi; all 22 otel-demo pods are Running/Ready with restart counts of 0 (fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-xdwst has 1).

Service frontend (ClusterIP 100.70.32.128, port 8080) has exactly one endpoint, pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-ssc7t at 100.96.4.88 on node i-029c97e90b3730286, and that single address is what frontend-proxy DNATs to; there is no second or stale endpoint behind the frontend Service.

No rollout or rescheduling touched the frontend during the window: the only frontend ReplicaSet is frontend-675fd7b5c5, created 2026-11-18T01:56:10Z and owned by Deployment frontend, holding the same pod that is running now; no second ReplicaSet for frontend exists.

The frontend pod is CPU-throttled but steadily so: its container CPU usage is 0.061–0.066 cores against the 100m limit, and the throttled-period share for pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-ssc7t stays between 0.28 and 0.37 at every 2-minute step from 02:16 to 02:52Z, with no step at the alert anchor 02:35:08Z.

Frontend latency shows no step change in the observed window: p99 of frontend span_name="GET" is 600–984 ms at every 2-minute step from 02:12 to 02:52Z, and over the last 30 minutes p95 is frontend 334 ms versus ad 60 ms, cart 92 ms, recommendation 78 ms, currency 81 ms and product-catalog 1.9 ms.

The only chaos in the window is a Chaos Mesh Schedule named otel-demo-fraud-detection-kafka-network-partition: each minute from 02:33:07Z to 02:45:07Z it spawns a NetworkChaos object (e.g. ...-h9m5q, -tfltv, -8f5gf) with "Successfully apply chaos" for otel-demo/fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-kqd2b, otel-demo/fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-xdwst and otel-demo/kafka-ff7884766-29vm9, then TimeUp/Recovered about 55 s later; it never names frontend or frontend-proxy.

No fault-injection setting referring to frontend is switched on: in ConfigMap flagd-config (key demo.flagd.json) every flag has defaultVariant "off" — including adFailure, cartFailure, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, imageSlowLoad (frontend image load delay = off), loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, kafkaQueueProblems, adHighCpu, adManualGc and emailMemoryLeak. Deployment env vars of frontend and frontend-proxy contain no failure/latency injection variable.

Grouped events over the authorized window show no Evicted, OOMKilling, BackOff, Failed or Unhealthy reason for any otel-demo Pod: in otel-demo the only Pod events are Created/Pulled/Started (1 each) plus 75 PodNetworkChaos Updated events, and the only Warning events in the cluster are in namespace data-recorders (2 FailedScheduling, 1 VolumeFailedDelete). All five nodes are Ready with MemoryPressure/DiskPressure/PIDPressure False.

A query for networkpolicies in namespace otel-demo returned an empty list, so no NetworkPolicy object was found to explain the resets; a service/endpoint query returned the single healthy frontend endpoint described above.

The 503/UC responses are most likely an HTTP/1.1 keep-alive reuse race: the frontend's Node HTTP server closed an idle connections, and frontend-proxy sent a request on that already-closed connection, giving response detail upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}, 0 upstream bytes and no frontend span. This would fit the sporadic, route-independent, low-rate pattern, but it cannot be confirmed because the Envoy route/retry/keep-alive configuration and the frontend server's keepAliveTimeout are baked into the container images and I could not read them.

A second candidate is CPU saturation of the frontend: it uses 0.061–0.066 cores of a 100m limit and 28–37% of its CFS periods are throttled, which could cause occasional connection drops under 50 concurrent load-generator users. Counter-evidence: the throttling and latency are flat across the entire observed window and do not change at the alert anchor, so this would be a standing condition rather than the event that made the alert fire.

Rejected: that the Chaos Mesh fraud-detection↔kafka network partition is the cause of this frontend-proxy alert. That experiment only names fraud-detection pods and kafka-ff7884766-29vm9 and runs 02:33:07–02:45:07Z, whereas frontend-proxy 503s are already logged at 02:25:01Z, 02:28:29Z and 02:29:17Z, before the first Applied event, and the 5-minute error-span increase dropped during the chaos windows (1.25, 0, 0, 1.10, 2.22 spans) versus 2.22–4.44 spans just before 02:33Z; GET / and /api/products requests do not traverse checkout/fraud-detection.

Rejected: frontend pod failure, restart, OOM or eviction as the mechanism — the pod is Running/Ready with restartCount 0, has no previous container instance, its ReplicaSet was created at 01:56:10Z with no later rollout, and no otel-demo Pod event carries reason Evicted, OOMKilling, BackOff, Failed or Unhealthy in the authorized window.

Other error series in the environment are background and not tied to this alert: ad, fraud-detection and recommendation show a constant ~1.05–2.11 errors per 10 minutes on span_name "flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream" (and recommendation "/flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream") at every step from 02:21Z onward, including steps where frontend-proxy error increase is 0; checkout, currency and product-catalog error series are 0. No other service's own error evidence is observed.

Check the frontend-proxy Envoy route configuration for its upstream (frontend) pool and add retry_on reset / raise the upstream idle timeout so that a keep-alive race cannot surface as a 503 to users, and compare the frontend container's Node keepAliveTimeout with the default demo configuration; that config is inside the images and was not readable here.

Review the RequestErrorRate rule's expression and threshold: the annotation value 0.0111 (=1/90) could not be reproduced from the available span metrics, where frontend-proxy ingress errors are about 1–4 spans per 5 minutes against ~3000 ingress spans per 5 minutes; confirming the rule's window and denominator is needed before treating such a low absolute error count as an alert-worthy condition.

gaps: The alert rule RequestErrorRate could not be read: list_prometheus_rules with rule_name="RequestErrorRate" returned nothing and an unfiltered list of rules returned no rule groups, so the alert's expression, window and 0.0111 figure are unknown and could not be reconciled with the observed span error counts (alert rules may live in a source not integrated in this Run).

The frontend container produced no stdout/stderr lines at all for 01:56:00–02:52:38Z (fetch_pod_logs returned 0 lines for every window tried), so no application log evidence exists to confirm or reject a frontend-side abort, exception or timeout; this is unavailable data, not proof that the frontend logged nothing.

The frontend-proxy access-log read hit the 4 MiB limit and stopped at 2026-11-18T02:39:49Z, so 503 lines after that time and the total count of 503s in the whole window are unknown; the 9 lines shown are a sample, not a rate.

Trace metrics for frontend-proxy begin at 02:11:38Z, so whether these 503/UC responses existed before that time (and whether their rate changed near the 02:35:08Z alert anchor) is unknown; the earliest authorization started 2026-11-17T02:52:38Z but no metric samples were returned before 02:11:38Z.

The mechanism that makes the frontend terminate connections is undetermined: the frontend server's HTTP keep-alive/request-timeout settings, and the frontend-proxy Envoy route retry/timeout/outlier config, are inside container images and were not readable (only four ConfigMaps exist in otel-demo and none is an Envoy or frontend config), and no packet capture or TCP-reset counters exist to confirm a reset.

No change record exists for this window: the change_history integration is not available in this Run, so when or how the frontend's connection behaviour started cannot be checked against a change timeline.

Consequences beyond frontend-proxy's own 503 count (for example which load-generator users were affected, or whether any real user workflow was lost) were not measured; the failing requests are seen only in the sampled proxy logs and sampled traces.
next_steps: Obtain and inspect the frontend-proxy Envoy route/upstream-http configuration (retry policy, upstream idle timeout, max connections) and the frontend container's Node HTTP server keep-alive/headers timeout settings, which are baked into ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-frontend-proxy and :2.1.3-frontend.
Fetch the RequestErrorRate alerting rule definition from the rule source that Alertmanager evaluates, and confirm its window/denominator against frontend-proxy ingress span counts.
Consider raising the frontend container's cpu limit (currently 100m while it uses 0.061–0.066 cores with 28–37% CFS throttling) and re-check whether the 503/UC rate falls.

If the resets continue, capture TCP resets on the frontend pod (or enable Envoy debug logging of upstream disconnect reasons) to distinguish a keep-alive reuse race from a kernel-level connection drop.
